summary.business: Cummins India Limited operates as a subsidiary of Cummins Inc., USA, focusing on the design, manufacture, and sale of diesel and natural gas engines, power generation systems, and related spare parts. The company serves a broad range of customers across industrial, automotive, and power generation sectors, leveraging its parent's global technology and brand. Its operations are supported by a network of manufacturing facilities and a joint venture in lubricants, along with an associate in alternator manufacturing.

currentContext.strengths: Technology and brand leadership through parent Cummins Inc., ensuring high product reliability and switching costs.|Integrated manufacturing and distribution network with a strong presence in power generation and industrial engines.|Strategic joint venture (Valvoline Cummins) and associate (CGTIPL) providing complementary products like lubricants and alternators.
currentContext.strategies: Investing in engineering capability, advanced and multi-pathway technologies, digital enablement and talent to develop solutions supporting the energy transition.|Strengthening manufacturing excellence, enhancing supply chain responsiveness and deepening customer engagement.|Expanding footprint across industrial segments through landmark wins, strong execution and investments in next-generation technologies.|Delivering compliant, lower-emission and fuel-efficient solutions while improving resource efficiency and advancing practical decarbonization pathways.|Dividend Distribution Policy: final dividend recommended in accordance with the principles and criteria set out in the Dividend Distribution Policy of the Company.|Reduce absolute Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions from facilities and operations by 50% by 2030|Achieve zero waste growth and minimize single-use plastics in facilities and operations by 2030 (2018 baseline)|Achieve gender diversity of 50% in the permanent employee category by 2040|Achieve 25% representation from candidates in aspirational districts through the education assistance program by FY 2029-30|Cover 10 new villages every year in aspirational districts by FY 2029-30|Continue to equip 5,000 students every year on life and employability skills by FY 2029-30

The company also generated 60,08,042 kWh of electricity from existing and new onsite solar installations across its facilities, including the Kothrud Engine Plant (4,400 kWp capacity), Power Generation Plant at Phaltan, Megasite at Phaltan, and Cummins Residential Campus.
currentContext.mdna: India's growth continues to be driven by infrastructure investment, manufacturing expansion, digital infrastructure and resilient domestic demand.|Geopolitical developments, shifting trade patterns and evolving supply chains have created uncertainty, particularly in export markets, but have reinforced India's position as a key growth and manufacturing hub.|Customer expectations are evolving toward more dependable, compliant and digitally enabled solutions that deliver performance and lifecycle value.|Sustained strong demand in PowerGen exports, with High Horsepower PowerGen products leading the charge, driven by realty and manufacturing segments.|Robust demand for Diesel Electric Tower Cars, Power Car diesel alternator sets and engines for Track Maintenance Machines driving record Rail revenue.|Strong momentum in City Gas Distribution network expansion driving supply of gas compression engines in Oil and Gas segment.|Record order intake in marine segment alongside highest-ever annual sales.|Secured multi-year orders for Track Maintenance Machine engines from Indian Railways.|Secured key orders from large mining OEMs in surface mining, dump trucks, excavators, motor graders, dozers and stone crusher applications.|Secured new orders for specialized vehicle applications from defence OEMs.|Continued execution of large orders for multiple hyperscale data centers coming up in India.

risks.note: As India advances toward a low-carbon future, the company must continuously innovate to provide cleaner, smarter power solutions. Failure to keep pace with the energy transition could erode its competitive position.

risks.risk: Climate change and environmental compliance risk
risks.note: The company has set absolute GHG reduction and zero waste targets. Stricter environmental regulations or failure to meet its own sustainability goals could lead to reputational damage, penalties, or increased operational costs.

risks.risk: Supply chain and manufacturing concentration risk
risks.note: The company relies on deep engineering expertise and strong manufacturing and supply chain capabilities. Disruptions in its concentrated manufacturing footprint or supply chain could materially impact operations.

risks.risk: Joint venture and associate dependency risk
risks.note: A significant portion of consolidated performance comes from its joint venture (Valvoline Cummins) and associate (Cummins Generator Technologies). Any deterioration in these relationships or their performance would directly impact consolidated results.
The company has set an ambitious goal of 50% gender diversity in permanent employees by 2040. Inability to attract, retain, and develop diverse talent could hinder innovation and long-term growth.

thesis (one-liner): Cummins India is a high-payout, net-cash market leader riding a structural domestic power-gen upcycle, with **data-center gensets (30–35% of domestic powergen)** as the marquee growth driver on top of CPCB-IV+ content gains, a fast-growing 20%+ distribution/aftermarket annuity, and a steady-but-cautious export book — guidance for FY27 is deliberately "moderate growth across segments" given commodity inflation and geopolitics.
scorecard:
**Full-year FY26 (vs FY25):**
| Metric | FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Net sales | ₹11,950 cr | +18% | from ₹10,166 cr |
| Domestic sales | ₹9,961 cr | +19% | broad-based |
| Exports | ₹1,989 cr | +12% | HHP ₹984 cr (+20%), LHP ₹807 cr (+3%) |
| PBT (pre-exceptional) | ₹3,104 cr | +24% | margin-accretive growth |
| PBT (post-exceptional) | ₹3,054 cr | +22% | exceptional ≈ -₹50 cr (FY) |

**FY26 domestic segment split:**
- Power Generation: ₹4,758 cr (+24%)
- Distribution: ₹3,278 cr (+22%)
- Industrial: ₹1,650 cr (-1%, marginally lower)

**Q4 FY26 (vs Q4 FY25 / vs Q3 FY26):**
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY | QoQ | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Net sales | ₹2,963 cr | +23% | -1% | vs ₹2,414 cr YoY; ₹3,006 cr QoQ |
| Domestic | ₹2,513 cr | +30% | -1% | |
| Exports | ₹450 cr | -6% | -5% | weak vs strong base |
| PBT (pre-exc.) | ₹820 cr | +20% | +14% | |
| PBT (post-exc.) | ₹852 cr | +25% | +44% | Q4 exceptional ≈ +₹32 cr (gain) |

**Q4 FY26 segment split (domestic):**
- Power Generation: ₹1,294 cr (+48% YoY, +21% QoQ) — strongest engine
- Distribution: ₹766 cr (+21% YoY, -18% QoQ)
- Industrial: ₹381 cr (+1% YoY, -18% QoQ)
- Exports HHP: ₹217 cr (-1% YoY, -7% QoQ); LHP: ₹127 cr (-18% YoY, -5% QoQ)

**Q4 powergen sub-split:** LHP ₹55 cr; medium-range ₹177 cr; heavy-duty ₹108 cr; remainder HHP (~₹954 cr, of which Hyperscaler ≈ ₹250 cr).
**Q4 industrial sub-split:** construction ₹164 cr; rail ₹111 cr; compressor ₹59 cr; remainder mining + defence.

**One-offs / quality flags:** Growth described as **predominantly volume-led** (mgmt: CPCB-IV+ price/content add is part, but HHP + industrial + distribution make it "actually volume led growth"). CPCB-IV+ prebuy not flagged as a one-off this quarter; transition now stable. Exceptional items small (-₹50 cr FY / +₹32 cr Q4 implied). Net-cash balance sheet (not quantified on call; structurally cash-rich, no major capex plan).
guidance (critical):
- **Revenue growth FY27:** "Moderate growth across segments" — explicitly NOT quantified; mgmt declined low-double-digit / mid-teens / high-single-digit framing. Domestic demand "robust" (inquiries + order book), but cautious on commodity inflation + geopolitics.
- **Margin:** No explicit margin guidance. Mgmt insists data-center/CPCB-IV+ growth is NOT materially margin-dilutive because localization content is "already very high" even on imported-engine products; pricing "largely sustaining" post CPCB-IV+ (30–35% price hike absorbed). HHP range positioned as higher-value.
- **Export outlook:** Cautious — "difficult to put fingers down" given geopolitics. Europe + Asia-Pac growing modestly; Middle East & others soft. No structural change in trend.
- **Data-center demand:** Very strong. ≈30–35% of domestic powergen (FY26), ~35% Q4. Inquiry velocity up sharply since Oct-2025, led by Colo, with Hyperscalers also building. Near-term (2–3 yrs) demand from Colo stays on localized QSK60 — clear line of sight. Installed base view referenced: ~1.5GW → 6–10GW potential. Order-to-delivery ~6–12 months before site ready; revenue recognized on genset installation.
demand / pipeline:
- Domestic demand "robust" across powergen/industrial/distribution; order book strong.
- Data center inquiry velocity sharply up since Oct-2025 (Colo > Hyperscalers, but both growing); large competitor orders being finalized (Perkins, Baudouin, Adani referenced by analyst).
- Non-data-center powergen demand: solar-cell manufacturing plants, pharma, quick-commerce dark stores, luxury residential & commercial realty — all showing good inquiries/orders. Non-DC powergen grew "higher double digits" in FY26.
- Industrial: railways performing very well (good order book); mining picked up last 6 months (tender velocity recovering); construction moderate (road-construction-linked); compressor entering cyclical down-leg.
segment commentary:
- **PowerGen (₹4,758 cr FY, +24%):** Star segment, data-center-led + broad-based (manufacturing, pharma, realty, quick-commerce). Q4 +48% YoY. Data center 30–35% of domestic powergen.
- **Industrial (₹1,650 cr FY, -1%):** Soft full-year; rail strong & sustaining, mining recovering, construction moderate, compressor down-cycle.
- **Distribution / aftermarket (₹3,278 cr FY, +22%):** Growth solutions-led, NOT price-led — service packages, predictive maintenance, dual-fuel kits, retrofit emission devices, parts beyond engines. CPCB-IV+ engines coming out of warranty from June onwards = annuity opportunity via extended-warranty schemes. Separate dedicated data-center aftermarket focus (99.99% uptime) over-and-above the 30–35% powergen DC number (not quantified).
- **Exports (₹1,989 cr FY, +12%):** HHP ₹984 cr (+20%); LHP ₹807 cr (+3%). Europe/Asia-Pac modest growth; Middle East soft. India base used for component sourcing into global DC engine builds.
growth / optionality:
- **Data-center HHP gensets:** QSK60 (localized) dominant for next 2–3 yrs; may shift toward 78L (more likely) and 95L over time — would re-evaluate India localization as volumes build. 95L not made by anyone in India (all imported, built in US).
- **Parent capacity:** Cummins Inc. investing ~$450m to add ~20GW capacity by 2030 (DC-focused) → expected to crunch import lead-times for QSK78/95 (lead-times have risen materially given global DC demand).
- **Exports leverage:** India supply base sourced into global DC builds.
- **New fuels / BESS:** Strong interest & inquiries in Battery Energy Storage Systems but no meaningful sales yet; NO local supply chain (import-dependent today), working on localization; positive long-term outlook, contribution un-quantifiable. Parent's gas/peak-shaving prime-mover product seen as US-specific — NOT an India opportunity. Other allied power solutions under evaluation (nothing to share yet).
margins & cost:
- Margins protected — high localization content even on imported-engine DC/CPCB-IV+ products; data-center/CPCB-IV+ growth "not impacting margins dramatically."
- Commodity inflation a headwind (incl. ~doubling of DEF / Diesel Exhaust Fluid prices, though DEF a very small share of distribution). Price hikes passed on with a lag and friction; CPCB-IV+ 30–35% price increase has sustained.
- Industry-wide supply constraints: supplier labour shortages, fuel-cost increments, war-related logistics delays.
capex: - Capacity utilization ~70% (combined powergen+industrial facilities). NO major capex plan; >₹1,000 cr invested over last 5 years on modernization + line-capability expansion (more output per line). Global integrated supply chain tapped for incremental output. Asset-light growth via productivity, not big greenfield.
capital allocation: - Structurally net-cash, high-payout profile (consistent with history; not explicitly quantified on this call). Continuous modest capex; no large outlay planned. (Dividend specifics not discussed on call.)
risks:
- Commodity inflation + DEF cost spikes; pass-through lag on pre-booked orders.
- Geopolitical / war-driven logistics delays and uncertainty (esp. exports).
- Demand elasticity below HHP (CPCB-IV+ range, short lead-times) if inflation worsens — HHP/project demand stays inelastic.
- Long-term mix shift to imported 78L/95L DC engines could narrow Cummins' localization cost-advantage vs peers (Perkins, Baudouin) all on imports — though mgmt argues whole-solution value proposition, not price, wins.
- Rising lead-times on imported nodes/engines due to global DC demand outpacing capacity.
- Competition poaching senior talent from Cummins (mgmt downplays).
management tone: Confident and measured. Bullish on domestic/data-center structural demand and distribution annuity; deliberately conservative on FY27 ("moderate growth," repeated caution on commodities/geopolitics). Guarded on quantification — declined to give DC sub-revenue, currency-depreciation split, lead-time numbers, BESS contribution, exact margins. Emphasizes value-proposition / end-to-end solution moat over pure price competition.
non-obvious insights:
- India DC share of powergen (30–35%) is structured differently from parent's "25%" (parent number is share of broader business, not powergen-only; parent's powergen-only DC share is much higher). India DC market only started accelerating Oct-2025; US/China far ahead — big optionality if India catches up.
- CPCB-IV+ engines exiting warranty (from June 2026) = new high-margin distribution/aftermarket annuity ("encircle the customer," extended-warranty schemes) on sophisticated after-treatment tech.
- Hyperscaler revenue Q4 ≈ ₹250 cr (vs implied HHP ~₹954 cr) — Colo still the bigger driver.
- Luxury-residential realty growth does NOT lift per-unit backup-power intensity — stays "backup," no scale change in utilization.
- BESS is import-dependent with no local supply chain yet — a gap vs the structural BESS push in India.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ✅ **Data-center buildout (Colo + Hyperscaler):** Cummins India direct beneficiary via QSK60/HHP gensets + dedicated DC aftermarket.
- ✅ **CPCB-IV+ out-of-warranty wave (Jun-2026 onward):** boosts distribution/aftermarket annuity.
- ⭐ **Parent's 20GW / $450m capacity add by 2030:** could shorten import lead-times → faster India DC fulfilment, but also enables imported 78/95L that may pressure local cost-edge.
- ⭐ **Solar-cell / pharma / quick-commerce / realty capex:** secondary powergen demand pools.

---
qoq log: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Sales ₹2,963 cr (+23% YoY, -1% QoQ); domestic +30% YoY; PowerGen ₹1,294 cr (+48% YoY); DC ~35% of domestic powergen (Hyperscaler ~₹250 cr); exports weak (₹450 cr, -6% YoY). FY26 sales ₹11,950 cr (+18%), PBT pre-exc ₹3,104 cr (+24%). FY27 guidance: "moderate growth across segments," cautious on commodities/geopolitics. Util ~70%, no major capex. BESS interest but no sales/local supply. CPCB-IV+ out-of-warranty annuity emerging from Jun-2026.

themes.title: Data-Center & AI electrical/cooling buildout
themes.need: AI/data-center capex pulls transformers, switchgear, gensets, HVAC/cooling, optical and cabling AND a new high-margin cooling supply chain. CUMMINSIND flags DC at ~30-35% of domestic powergen with a demand surge since Oct-2025; VENUSPIPES won a ~INR185cr DC-cooling LOI; AEROFLEX building liquid-cooling skids; BLUESTARCO on DC MEP; STLTECH/NETWEB on optical + HPC/AI servers (STLTECH's DC+Enterprise mix hit 21% of Q1FY27 revenue from 1% in FY26 on record INR13,100cr quarterly order intake anchored by a $1.1bn multi-year hyperscaler deal; FY27 EBITDA-margin guide raised 20%->23% and DC+Enterprise mix guide raised 30%->50% of revenue); REDINGTON/DCI/IVALUE on GPU/AI-infra distribution. Q1FY27 added two balance-sheet-scale entrants: HCLTECH is putting up to INR 3,500cr into its own AI-datacenter business with a 50MW long-term ambition ('megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor'), and RELIANCE disclosed a 168 MW Meta data centre at Jamnagar built on its own balance sheet.
themes.driver: DC cooling LOIs converting (VENUSPIPES, AEROFLEX); hyperscaler/colo India capex (CUMMINSIND gensets, BLUESTARCO MEP); STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler optical-connectivity deal and 2.4x QoQ order-book jump to INR18,618cr; GPU/AI-infra orders.

themes.title: Capital-goods & machine-tool import-substitution
themes.need: Atmanirbhar machine-tool and heavy-engineering localization is supply-constrained against import-substituting demand. JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).

themes.title: Power generation & utilities - baseload + new capacity
themes.need: Record peak demand and a thermal+hydro+nuclear capacity-addition cycle underpin regulated and merchant generators plus their service chain. NTPC/JSWENERGY/TATAPOWER/TORNTPOWER/ADANIPOWER add thermal + RE; NHPC/SJVN/NLCINDIA on hydro/lignite; TRITURBINE/TDPOWERSYS/GVPIL on turbines/generators & aftermarket; POWERMECH on EPC + O&M.
themes.driver: Peak-demand/PLF strength; new-unit commissioning; FGD + thermal-aftermarket order conversion.

hero.oneLiner: Cummins India is a high-payout, net-cash market leader riding a structural domestic power-gen upcycle, with **data-center gensets (30–35% of domestic powergen)** as the marquee growth driver on top of CPCB-IV+ content gains, a fast-growing 20%+ distribution/aftermarket annuity, and a steady-but-cautious export book — guidance for FY27 is deliberately "moderate growth across segments" given commodity inflation and geopolitics.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Cummins India Limited operates as a subsidiary of Cummins Inc., USA, focusing on the design, manufacture, and sale of diesel and natural gas engines, power generation systems, and related spare parts. The company serves a broad range of customers across industrial, automotive, and power generation sectors, leveraging its parent's global technology and brand. Its operations are supported by a network of manufacturing facilities and a joint venture in lubricants, along with an associate in alternator manufacturing.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Cummins Sales & Service Private Limited (CSSPL) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary; 100% stake sold effective April 01, 2025, ceased to be a subsidiary.
- Valvoline Cummins Private Limited (VCPL) — JV: 50:50 joint venture with Valvoline International Inc., USA, engaged in lubricants and engine oils.
- Cummins Generator Technologies India Private Limited (CGTIPL) — associate: Associate company with 48.74% shareholding; engaged in design, manufacturing, marketing, sales and service of alternators and related spare parts.
- Clean Max Yellowstone Private Limited (Clean Max) — associate: Special Purpose Vehicle; 8.78% equity stake acquired for procuring renewable power (Solar/wind).

segment_detail.title: Segment commentary
segment_detail.body:
- **PowerGen (₹4,758 cr FY, +24%):** Star segment, data-center-led + broad-based (manufacturing, pharma, realty, quick-commerce). Q4 +48% YoY. Data center 30–35% of domestic powergen.
- **Industrial (₹1,650 cr FY, -1%):** Soft full-year; rail strong & sustaining, mining recovering, construction moderate, compressor down-cycle.
- **Distribution / aftermarket (₹3,278 cr FY, +22%):** Growth solutions-led, NOT price-led — service packages, predictive maintenance, dual-fuel kits, retrofit emission devices, parts beyond engines. CPCB-IV+ engines coming out of warranty from June onwards = annuity opportunity via extended-warranty schemes. Separate dedicated data-center aftermarket focus (99.99% uptime) over-and-above the 30–35% powergen DC number (not quantified).
- **Exports (₹1,989 cr FY, +12%):** HHP ₹984 cr (+20%); LHP ₹807 cr (+3%). Europe/Asia-Pac modest growth; Middle East soft. India base used for component sourcing into global DC engine builds.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Engines:** Diesel Engines, Natural Gas Engines
- **Power Generation:** Generator Sets, Alternators (via Associate CGTIPL)
- **Components:** Spare Parts
- **Lubricants (via JV VCPL):** Lubricants, Engine Oils

order_book.title: Demand / Pipeline
order_book.body:
- Domestic demand "robust" across powergen/industrial/distribution; order book strong.
- Data center inquiry velocity sharply up since Oct-2025 (Colo > Hyperscalers, but both growing); large competitor orders being finalized (Perkins, Baudouin, Adani referenced by analyst).
- Non-data-center powergen demand: solar-cell manufacturing plants, pharma, quick-commerce dark stores, luxury residential & commercial realty — all showing good inquiries/orders. Non-DC powergen grew "higher double digits" in FY26.
- Industrial: railways performing very well (good order book); mining picked up last 6 months (tender velocity recovering); construction moderate (road-construction-linked); compressor entering cyclical down-leg.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue growth FY27:** "Moderate growth across segments" — explicitly NOT quantified; mgmt declined low-double-digit / mid-teens / high-single-digit framing. Domestic demand "robust" (inquiries + order book), but cautious on commodity inflation + geopolitics.
- **Margin:** No explicit margin guidance. Mgmt insists data-center/CPCB-IV+ growth is NOT materially margin-dilutive because localization content is "already very high" even on imported-engine products; pricing "largely sustaining" post CPCB-IV+ (30–35% price hike absorbed). HHP range positioned as higher-value.
- **Export outlook:** Cautious — "difficult to put fingers down" given geopolitics. Europe + Asia-Pac growing modestly; Middle East & others soft. No structural change in trend.
- **Data-center demand:** Very strong. ≈30–35% of domestic powergen (FY26), ~35% Q4. Inquiry velocity up sharply since Oct-2025, led by Colo, with Hyperscalers also building. Near-term (2–3 yrs) demand from Colo stays on localized QSK60 — clear line of sight. Installed base view referenced: ~1.5GW → 6–10GW potential. Order-to-delivery ~6–12 months before site ready; revenue recognized on genset installation.

growth_optionality.title: Growth / Optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Data-center HHP gensets:** QSK60 (localized) dominant for next 2–3 yrs; may shift toward 78L (more likely) and 95L over time — would re-evaluate India localization as volumes build. 95L not made by anyone in India (all imported, built in US).
- **Parent capacity:** Cummins Inc. investing ~$450m to add ~20GW capacity by 2030 (DC-focused) → expected to crunch import lead-times for QSK78/95 (lead-times have risen materially given global DC demand).
- **Exports leverage:** India supply base sourced into global DC builds.
- **New fuels / BESS:** Strong interest & inquiries in Battery Energy Storage Systems but no meaningful sales yet; NO local supply chain (import-dependent today), working on localization; positive long-term outlook, contribution un-quantifiable. Parent's gas/peak-shaving prime-mover product seen as US-specific — NOT an India opportunity. Other allied power solutions under evaluation (nothing to share yet).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's growth continues to be driven by infrastructure investment, manufacturing expansion, digital infrastructure and resilient domestic demand.
- Geopolitical developments, shifting trade patterns and evolving supply chains have created uncertainty, particularly in export markets, but have reinforced India's position as a key growth and manufacturing hub.
- Customer expectations are evolving toward more dependable, compliant and digitally enabled solutions that deliver performance and lifecycle value.
- Sustained strong demand in PowerGen exports, with High Horsepower PowerGen products leading the charge, driven by realty and manufacturing segments.
- Robust demand for Diesel Electric Tower Cars, Power Car diesel alternator sets and engines for Track Maintenance Machines driving record Rail revenue.
- Strong momentum in City Gas Distribution network expansion driving supply of gas compression engines in Oil and Gas segment.
- Record order intake in marine segment alongside highest-ever annual sales.
- Secured multi-year orders for Track Maintenance Machine engines from Indian Railways.
- Secured key orders from large mining OEMs in surface mining, dump trucks, excavators, motor graders, dozers and stone crusher applications.
- Secured new orders for specialized vehicle applications from defence OEMs.
- Continued execution of large orders for multiple hyperscale data centers coming up in India.

margins.title: Margins & Cost
margins.body:
- Margins protected — high localization content even on imported-engine DC/CPCB-IV+ products; data-center/CPCB-IV+ growth "not impacting margins dramatically."
- Commodity inflation a headwind (incl. ~doubling of DEF / Diesel Exhaust Fluid prices, though DEF a very small share of distribution). Price hikes passed on with a lag and friction; CPCB-IV+ 30–35% price increase has sustained.
- Industry-wide supply constraints: supplier labour shortages, fuel-cost increments, war-related logistics delays.

capital_allocation.title: Capital Allocation
capital_allocation.body: - Structurally net-cash, high-payout profile (consistent with history; not explicitly quantified on this call). Continuous modest capex; no large outlay planned. (Dividend specifics not discussed on call.)

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY26, Cummins India continued to invest in renewable energy procurement by acquiring an 8.78% equity stake in Clean Max Yellowstone Private Limited, a Special Purpose Vehicle, for procuring renewable power (solar/wind/hybrid) for its factories and premises. The company also generated 60,08,042 kWh of electricity from existing and new onsite solar installations across its facilities, including the Kothrud Engine Plant (4,400 kWp capacity), Power Generation Plant at Phaltan, Megasite at Phaltan, and Cummins Residential Campus.

management_tone.title: Management Tone
management_tone.body: Confident and measured. Bullish on domestic/data-center structural demand and distribution annuity; deliberately conservative on FY27 ("moderate growth," repeated caution on commodities/geopolitics). Guarded on quantification — declined to give DC sub-revenue, currency-depreciation split, lead-time numbers, BESS contribution, exact margins. Emphasizes value-proposition / end-to-end solution moat over pure price competition.

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": false, "note": "No material litigation disclosed. A minor non-compliance penalty of H 2,360 was paid to stock exchanges for a one-day delay in audit committee composition.", "as_of": "2026-07-20"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Technology and brand leadership through parent Cummins Inc., ensuring high product reliability and switching costs.
- Integrated manufacturing and distribution network with a strong presence in power generation and industrial engines.
- Strategic joint venture (Valvoline Cummins) and associate (CGTIPL) providing complementary products like lubricants and alternators.

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- Commodity inflation + DEF cost spikes; pass-through lag on pre-booked orders.
- Geopolitical / war-driven logistics delays and uncertainty (esp. exports).
- Demand elasticity below HHP (CPCB-IV+ range, short lead-times) if inflation worsens — HHP/project demand stays inelastic.
- Long-term mix shift to imported 78L/95L DC engines could narrow Cummins' localization cost-advantage vs peers (Perkins, Baudouin) all on imports — though mgmt argues whole-solution value proposition, not price, wins.
- Rising lead-times on imported nodes/engines due to global DC demand outpacing capacity.
- Competition poaching senior talent from Cummins (mgmt downplays).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious insights
non_obvious.body:
- India DC share of powergen (30–35%) is structured differently from parent's "25%" (parent number is share of broader business, not powergen-only; parent's powergen-only DC share is much higher). India DC market only started accelerating Oct-2025; US/China far ahead — big optionality if India catches up.
- CPCB-IV+ engines exiting warranty (from June 2026) = new high-margin distribution/aftermarket annuity ("encircle the customer," extended-warranty schemes) on sophisticated after-treatment tech.
- Hyperscaler revenue Q4 ≈ ₹250 cr (vs implied HHP ~₹954 cr) — Colo still the bigger driver.
- Luxury-residential realty growth does NOT lift per-unit backup-power intensity — stays "backup," no scale change in utilization.
- BESS is import-dependent with no local supply chain yet — a gap vs the structural BESS push in India.

challenges.title: Challenges → Beneficiaries
challenges.body:
- ✅ **Data-center buildout (Colo + Hyperscaler):** Cummins India direct beneficiary via QSK60/HHP gensets + dedicated DC aftermarket.
- ✅ **CPCB-IV+ out-of-warranty wave (Jun-2026 onward):** boosts distribution/aftermarket annuity.
- ⭐ **Parent's 20GW / $450m capacity add by 2030:** could shorten import lead-times → faster India DC fulfilment, but also enables imported 78/95L that may pressure local cost-edge.
- ⭐ **Solar-cell / pharma / quick-commerce / realty capex:** secondary powergen demand pools.

---

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Sales ₹2,963 cr (+23% YoY, -1% QoQ); domestic +30% YoY; PowerGen ₹1,294 cr (+48% YoY); DC ~35% of domestic powergen (Hyperscaler ~₹250 cr); exports weak (₹450 cr, -6% YoY). FY26 sales ₹11,950 cr (+18%), PBT pre-exc ₹3,104 cr (+24%). FY27 guidance: "moderate growth across segments," cautious on commodities/geopolitics. Util ~70%, no major capex. BESS interest but no sales/local supply. CPCB-IV+ out-of-warranty annuity emerging from Jun-2026.

other.body:

- [Document type] This is a press release on unaudited quarterly financial results issued under a stock-exchange intimation, not a structured investor slide deck; it carries no slides, charts, segment tables or capacity data.
